# VirtualList

Header: `winui/ui/collections/VirtualListControl.hpp`.

A list that scrolls itself and creates Elements only for the rows in view.

It asks its item factory for a fresh [Element](../tree/element.md) per visible index and drops rows as they scroll out, so a 100,000-item list holds about a dozen live controls. A [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll), by contrast, keeps its whole child and clips it. The visible rows are created again on every arrange and scroll step, so keep per-row state in the caller's data, not in the row. The list scrolls with the wheel and an overlay scroll bar. [TableView](table-view.md#uitableview)'s body is one. All rows share [item_height()](#item_height) unless [set_size_items_to_content()](#set_size_items_to_content) lets each row be as tall as it measures. It has no spec. For a list in a declared tree use [ui::ListView](list-view.md#uilistview). Build this one by hand when rows of one height, an index and a factory are all a list needs.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> names(1000, "Row"); // outlives the window

auto list = std::make_unique<ui::VirtualListControl>();
list->set_item_height(36.0f);
list->set_item_factory([&names](std::size_t i) -> std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> {
    return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(names[i]);
});
list->set_item_count(names.size());
ui::VirtualListControl* observer = window.set_content(std::move(list));
auto top_button = std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Top");
top_button->on_click([observer] { observer->set_scroll_offset(0.0f); }); // back to the top
```

## `ui::VirtualListControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ScrollProvider`.

A list that scrolls itself and creates Elements only for the rows in view.

It asks its item factory for a fresh [Element](../tree/element.md) per visible index and drops rows as they scroll out, so a 100,000-item list holds about a dozen live controls. A [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll), by contrast, keeps its whole child and clips it. The visible rows are created again on every arrange and scroll step, so keep per-row state in the caller's data, not in the row. The list scrolls with the wheel and an overlay scroll bar. [TableView](table-view.md#uitableview)'s body is one. All rows share [item_height()](#item_height) unless [set_size_items_to_content()](#set_size_items_to_content) lets each row be as tall as it measures. It has no spec. For a list in a declared tree use [ui::ListView](list-view.md#uilistview). Build this one by hand when rows of one height, an index and a factory are all a list needs.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> names(1000, "Row"); // outlives the window

auto list = std::make_unique<ui::VirtualListControl>();
list->set_item_height(36.0f);
list->set_item_factory([&names](std::size_t i) -> std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> {
    return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(names[i]);
});
list->set_item_count(names.size());
ui::VirtualListControl* observer = window.set_content(std::move(list));
auto top_button = std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Top");
top_button->on_click([observer] { observer->set_scroll_offset(0.0f); }); // back to the top
```

### ItemFactory

```cpp
using ui::VirtualListControl::ItemFactory = Callback<std::unique_ptr<Element>(std::size_t index)>
```

Builds the row for item `index`. The list takes ownership and destroys the row once it scrolls out of view.

### VirtualListControl

```cpp
VirtualListControl() = default
```

An empty list: no factory, no items, 32-DIP rows.

### set_item_factory

```cpp
void set_item_factory(ItemFactory factory)
```

Sets the factory that returns the [Element](../tree/element.md) for any index in [0, [item_count()](#item_count)). It is called for every visible row on each arrange and scroll step, so keep it cheap. Returning nullptr ends the realized rows there, for a source that shrank before [set_item_count()](#set_item_count) caught up. That row and the ones after it stay empty. Replacing the factory rebuilds the rows on the next layout.

### item_count

```cpp
std::size_t item_count() const
```

How many items the list scrolls over; 0 by default.

### set_item_count

```cpp
void set_item_count(std::size_t count)
```

Changes the item count and lays the list out again. The scroll offset is clamped again on the next arrange. Forgets the heights the rows measured.

### item_height

```cpp
float item_height() const
```

Every row's height in DIPs; 32 by default. Each row is arranged to exactly this height, whatever it measures. When the rows size to their content, it is the least height of a row and the estimate for a row not yet seen.

### set_item_height

```cpp
void set_item_height(float height)
```

Changes the row height, lays the list out again and forgets the heights the rows measured.

### size_items_to_content

```cpp
bool size_items_to_content() const
```

Whether each row is measured with unbounded height and is as tall as it asks for, at least [item_height()](#item_height). Off by default. A row keeps the height it measured while it is out of view, so scrolling back finds it where it was. Rows never seen count as [item_height()](#item_height).

### set_size_items_to_content

```cpp
void set_size_items_to_content(bool on)
```

Turns content-sized rows on or off and lays the list out again.

### forget_item_heights

```cpp
void forget_item_heights()
```

Forgets every height the rows measured and lays the list out again. Call it after a change that reflows the rows' content, such as a new column width. The list tracks its own width changes.

### item_top

```cpp
float item_top(std::size_t index) const
```

Where item `index` starts, in DIPs from the top of the content, leading space included.

### item_extent

```cpp
float item_extent(std::size_t index) const
```

Item `index`'s height. That is what it measured while the rows size to their content, and [item_height()](#item_height) otherwise.

### index_at

```cpp
std::size_t index_at(float y) const
```

The item at `y` DIPs from the top of the content. Returns [item_count()](#item_count) past the last item and 0 over the leading space.

### leading_space

```cpp
float leading_space() const
```

Room before the first item that scrolls with the content, where a [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) puts its header. The items start this far down the content, and the content is this much taller.

### set_leading_space

```cpp
void set_leading_space(float space)
```

Sets the leading space in DIPs, clamped to >= 0. Lays the list out again only on a change.

### content_height

```cpp
float content_height() const
```

The content's height: the leading space and every item.

### scroll_offset

```cpp
float scroll_offset() const
```

How far the content is scrolled, in DIPs from the top (0 is the top).

### set_scroll_offset

```cpp
void set_scroll_offset(float offset)
```

Sets the offset directly, for example to scroll to the top. Clamps it to the current content range and rebuilds the realized rows at once.

### right_gutter

```cpp
float right_gutter() const
```

The width the vertical bar takes from the rows, decided by [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure). It is the bar's gutter under a theme whose bar takes room of its own, while the content overflows. It is 0 for the overlay bar, which draws over the rows.

### viewport_rect

```cpp
Rect viewport_rect() const
```

Where the rows are shown: the bounds minus the right gutter.

### scroll_info

```cpp
std::optional<ScrollInfo> scroll_info() const override
```

[Element::scroll_info()](../tree/element.md#scroll_info), the same as a [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll)'s. It can be pulled a tenth of its viewport past either end.

### first_visible_index

```cpp
std::size_t first_visible_index() const
```

The item index of the first realized row. The realized items are [[first_visible_index()](#first_visible_index), [first_visible_index()](#first_visible_index) + [visible_count()](#visible_count)). [visible_item()](#visible_item) takes an offset into that range. Meant for inspection and testing, not for driving the list from outside.

### visible_count

```cpp
std::size_t visible_count() const
```

How many rows are realized right now: the rows at least partly in view.

### visible_item

```cpp
Element* visible_item(std::size_t i) const
```

The `i`th realized row; 0 is the row of [first_visible_index()](#first_visible_index). Throws std::out_of_range past [visible_count()](#visible_count). The list owns the row and destroys it when it scrolls out of view.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

The realized rows, top first. Only these can take focus. Focus does not scroll a row into view.

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

Reported to screen readers as a scrollable List without children, because only the visible rows exist as Elements.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers automation_providers() lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

### wheel_override

```cpp
bool wheel_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A wheel turn over this element ([handle_wheel()](../tree/element.md#handle_wheel)). Return true when it scrolled something here. Default: an element with no children hands it to [pointer_override()](#pointer_override) and returns false; one with children returns false.

### children_hit_clip

```cpp
std::optional<Rect> children_hit_clip() const override
```

Where the children can be hit, in this element's layout coordinates, or nullopt for anywhere (the default): a scrolling control returns its viewport, so content scrolled out of view is not hit.

### covers_children_at

```cpp
bool covers_children_at(Point p) const override
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Fades the scroll bar, then ticks the rows.
